jever.description: Frisian-bitter Pils with a strong hop bite and a very dry finish.
jever.humorousBio: Bitter. Dry. Not a beer for people who like their beer to apologise.
jever.disLikeQuip: You and Jever have a complicated past.

augustiner.description: Munich Helles with a soft malt note and gentle hops – the classic in the swing-top bottle.
augustiner.humorousBio: Needs no marketing. Has a queue.
augustiner.disLikeQuip: Brave. In Munich, people would be staring at you now.

paulaner-weisse.description: Cloudy Hefeweizen with banana, clove and a creamy head.
paulaner-weisse.humorousBio: Tastes of banana without ever having seen one.
paulaner-weisse.disLikeQuip: No banana for you. More for the beer garden.

becks.description: Bremen Pils, mildly bitter and exported worldwide.
becks.humorousBio: The mate who is already at every party. Somehow, always.
becks.disLikeQuip: Beck's will get over it. It has plenty of friends.

koestritzer.description: Thuringian Schwarzbier with roasted malt, coffee and chocolate notes – yet surprisingly light.
koestritzer.humorousBio: Looks like Guinness, drinks like Pils. A double agent.
koestritzer.disLikeQuip: The double agent has been exposed. Mission aborted.

ratsherrn.description: Hamburg Pale Ale with citrus and grapefruit aromas from American hop varieties.
ratsherrn.disLikeQuip: Too much grapefruit? We get it. Hamburg doesn't.

corona.description: Light Mexican lager, traditionally with a lime wedge in the neck.
corona.humorousBio: Without lime, just a beer. With lime, still just a beer.

schlenkerla.description: Bamberg Rauchbier from malt kilned over beechwood. Divisive since 1405.
schlenkerla.humorousBio: Tastes like a campfire with opinions.
schlenkerla.disLikeQuip: Understandable. You two never really stood a chance.

rothaus.description: Black Forest Pils in the 0.33 l bottle with the pine cone. Balanced between hops and malt.
rothaus.humorousBio: Small bottle, big fan club. Sold out exactly when you need it most.
rothaus.disLikeQuip: Tannenzäpfle is sad now. Somewhere in the Black Forest, a pine cone falls.

punk-ipa.description: The IPA that brought the craft beer boom to Europe. Tropical fruit, resin, bitterness.
punk-ipa.humorousBio: Caused a riot in 2007 and is now in the supermarket. Like all of us.
punk-ipa.disLikeQuip: Punk is dead. At least for you.

frueh.description: Top-fermented Kölsch from the Stange glass. Light, fresh, refilled without asking.
frueh.humorousBio: Comes in 0.2 l. Comes often, though.
frueh.disLikeQuip: Lid on the glass. The waiter got the message.

guinness.description: Irish dry stout with roasted notes, a creamy nitrogen head and a dry finish.
guinness.humorousBio: Takes 119.5 seconds to pour. And you're supposed to wait. The cheek.

salvator.description: The original Doppelbock. Malty, sweet, strong – the monks' Lenten beer since the 17th century.
salvator.humorousBio: Liquid bread. Invented by monks who cheated while fasting.
salvator.disLikeQuip: The monks are fasting without you now.

duvel.description: Belgian strong golden ale. Looks like a Pils, but has 8.5 % and a huge head.
duvel.humorousBio: Its name means “devil”. And that's not a joke.
duvel.disLikeQuip: The devil takes it personally. He has time.

krombacher.description: Mild Pils brewed with rock spring water, one of Germany's best-selling beers.
krombacher.humorousBio: Tastes of weekends and barbecue smoke. For everyone. Really everyone.
krombacher.disLikeQuip: Krombacher will cope. It has a few million other fans.

tegernseer.description: Upper Bavarian Helles, soft and round, one of the most drinkable beers in the country.
tegernseer.humorousBio: Soft as a Sunday morning by the lake. No alarm clock.
tegernseer.disLikeQuip: A no for Lake Tegernsee. The ducks are appalled.

astra.description: St. Pauli's neighbourhood beer. Mildly bitter Pils with the heart-and-anchor logo.
astra.humorousBio: Harbour front, heart, anchor. Not a beer for small talk.
astra.disLikeQuip: Astra takes it on the chin. Rule of the Kiez: no cheap shots.

veltins.description: Fresh, clear Sauerland Pils with a fine hop note.
veltins.humorousBio: Fresh, clear, uncomplicated. Like a firm handshake.
veltins.disLikeQuip: No handshake today. The Sauerland stays silent.

stoertebeker.description: Cloudy Kellerbier from the Baltic coast with a soft yeast and malt note.
stoertebeker.humorousBio: Unfiltered. Has nothing to hide – except yeast.
stoertebeker.disLikeQuip: Störtebeker will plunder someone else now.

bitburger.description: Finely bitter Pils from the Eifel with a pronounced hop note. “Bitte ein Bit.”
bitburger.humorousBio: Wears a suit. Even at the weekend.

radeberger.description: Saxon Pilsner in the Bohemian style, finely bitter with a noble hop bite.
radeberger.humorousBio: Finely bitter and a little proud of its own history. Rightly so.

flensburger.description: North German Pils with a strong hop bite and the famous plop of the swing top.
flensburger.humorousBio: Goes plop. Doesn't say much. Means it, though.
flensburger.disLikeQuip: No plop for you. Flensburg just shrugs.

urquell.description: The world's first Pilsner, brewed with Saaz hops since 1842. Full-bodied and spicy.
urquell.humorousBio: The original. And it knows it.
urquell.disLikeQuip: The original is unimpressed. It has survived worse.

warsteiner.description: Mild Sauerland Pils in the tulip glass. A queen among beers, says the advert.
warsteiner.humorousBio: Has a crown in its logo and still no airs and graces.
warsteiner.disLikeQuip: The crown is crooked. But it stays on.

erdinger.description: The world's largest wheat beer brewery. Mild, lively, with a fine yeast note.
erdinger.humorousBio: The wheat beer even your aunt knows. From TV.

weihenstephaner.description: From the world's oldest brewery. Full-bodied Hefeweizen with banana and clove, much decorated.
weihenstephaner.humorousBio: In business since 1040. More experience than you and me combined.
weihenstephaner.disLikeQuip: First no since 1040. The abbey archive has been informed.

gaffel.description: A slightly hoppier Kölsch with a dry finish.
gaffel.humorousBio: The Kölsch for people who still know what they're drinking at carnival.
gaffel.disLikeQuip: Gaffel goes to carnival without you. Alaaf anyway.

uerige.description: Düsseldorf's most bitter Altbier. Copper-coloured, well hopped, malt-forward.
uerige.humorousBio: “Dat lecker Dröppke”, says Düsseldorf. Cologne disagrees.
uerige.disLikeQuip: No lecker Dröppke. Cologne quietly applauds.

diebels.description: Mild Altbier classic from the Lower Rhine with a round malt body.
diebels.humorousBio: The Alt that gets on with everyone. Even with Kölsch drinkers.
diebels.disLikeQuip: Even Diebels can't please everyone. Surprise.

heineken.description: Dutch lager with a slightly sweet note. In the same green bottle worldwide.
heineken.humorousBio: Is everywhere. Tastes the same everywhere. That's the plan.
heineken.disLikeQuip: Heineken is everywhere. Just not with you.

stella.description: Belgian premium lager with a light malt sweetness, served in a chalice.
stella.humorousBio: Comes in a chalice. Feels like a champagne reception, but it's lager.
stella.disLikeQuip: No champagne reception today. The chalice stays empty.

leffe.description: Belgian abbey beer, sweetish, malty, with clove and vanilla.
leffe.humorousBio: Tastes like a dessert dressed up as a beer.

celebrator.description: Dark Doppelbock with chocolate, dried fruit and roasted malt. With a plastic goat on the neck.
celebrator.humorousBio: Has a little goat on the bottle. Needs no further arguments.
celebrator.disLikeQuip: The goat saw that. The goat never forgets.

drunken-sailor.description: Munich IPA with mango, grapefruit and plenty of bitterness. Craft from Bavaria, minus the purity-law debate.
drunken-sailor.humorousBio: Bavarian craft beer. Yes, that exists. And it's loud.
drunken-sailor.disLikeQuip: The sailor sails on. Without you on board.

sternburg.description: Leipzig export with a light malt sweetness. The corner-shop beer par excellence.
sternburg.humorousBio: Costs less than the deposit on it. And is still proud.
sternburg.disLikeQuip: You turned down a beer that costs less than its deposit. Respect.

oettinger.description: Bavarian discount Pils, mild and uncomplicated. No advertising, but cheap.
oettinger.humorousBio: Doesn't advertise. Doesn't have to. Everyone knows it from uni anyway.
oettinger.disLikeQuip: Oettinger is used to rejection. Just not on price.

hasseroeder.description: Harz Pils in a hexagonal bottle with a robust hop note.
hasseroeder.humorousBio: Hexagonal bottle. Because anyone can do round.

wernesgruener.description: Pils from the Vogtland with a pronounced but soft hop bitterness.
wernesgruener.humorousBio: Calls itself a legend. And who would argue with that.
wernesgruener.disLikeQuip: You argued with a legend. Brave.

hofbraeu.description: The Helles from the Hofbräuhaus – a bit hoppier than other Munich Helles.
hofbraeu.humorousBio: Photographed by more tourists per day than the Eiffel Tower. Or so it feels.
hofbraeu.disLikeQuip: One Prosit fewer. The tourists will drink it.

andechser-doppelbock.description: Dark abbey Doppelbock from the Holy Mountain. Malty, warm, with caramel and plum.
andechser-doppelbock.humorousBio: Brewed by monks. You can tell they have time.
andechser-doppelbock.disLikeQuip: The monks are praying for you. They have the time.

moenchshof-keller.description: Franconian Kellerbier, unfiltered, amber, with a strong malt body.
moenchshof-keller.humorousBio: Unfiltered and proud of it. Like a good friend after the third beer.

einbecker-urbock.description: From the town that gave Bock beer its name. Dark, malty, with a fine hop bitterness.
einbecker-urbock.humorousBio: Invented Bock beer. Mentions it now and then.
einbecker-urbock.disLikeQuip: The inventor of Bock is offended. For the first time since 1378.

jever-fun.description: Alcohol-free Pils with Jever's typical bitterness – just without the excuse.
jever-fun.humorousBio: As bitter as its big brother, but drives you home afterwards.
jever-fun.disLikeQuip: Not even without alcohol? That's honest.

erdinger-af.description: Alcohol-free wheat beer, lively and slightly sweet. Popular with people in running shoes.
erdinger-af.humorousBio: Drunk after the marathon. By people who mention it.
erdinger-af.disLikeQuip: No isotonic thirst-quenching today. The running club has been informed.

clausthaler.description: One of the classic alcohol-free beers – mildly bitter and unexcited.
clausthaler.humorousBio: Not always, but more and more often. You know the one.
clausthaler.disLikeQuip: Not always. And for you, apparently never.

schneider-tap7.description: Amber wheat beer with clove, caramel and bread crust. The original among the darker ones.
schneider-tap7.humorousBio: Wheat beer, but with life experience.
schneider-tap7.disLikeQuip: Too dark for a wheat beer? Schneider takes it with dignity.

franziskaner.description: Mild Munich Hefeweizen, fruity and creamy.
franziskaner.humorousBio: Wears a habit, but brings good vibes.
franziskaner.disLikeQuip: The monk on the label briefly looks away.

augustiner-edelstoff.description: Augustiner's export: full-bodied, soft, dangerously drinkable.
augustiner-edelstoff.humorousBio: Its name means “noble stuff”, and it takes that seriously.
augustiner-edelstoff.disLikeQuip: You turned down the Edelstoff. Munich will talk about it.

schoenramer-pils.description: Upper Bavarian Pils with plenty of hops – a favourite of beer nerds.
schoenramer-pils.humorousBio: Bavarian, but bitter. That really exists.
schoenramer-pils.disLikeQuip: The beer nerds' favourite. They're writing a blog post now.

brlo-pale-ale.description: Berlin Pale Ale with citrus and resin, brewed in a brewery made of shipping containers.
brlo-pale-ale.humorousBio: From Berlin. Has a podcast. Probably.
brlo-pale-ale.disLikeQuip: Berlin heard you. Berlin doesn't care.

maisel-pale-ale.description: Fruity Pale Ale from Bayreuth with apricot, mango and caramel.
maisel-pale-ale.humorousBio: Craft from Franconia. With friends, it says itself.
maisel-pale-ale.disLikeQuip: Maisel still has plenty of friends. Don't worry.

sierra-nevada.description: The forefather of American Pale Ale: Cascade hops, pine, grapefruit.
sierra-nevada.humorousBio: Invented craft beer before it was cool.
sierra-nevada.disLikeQuip: You turned down the grandad of craft. He won't tell anyone.

peroni.description: Light Italian lager, fresh and uncomplicated.

budvar.description: Bohemian lager with Saaz hops and long maturation. The real Budweiser.
budvar.humorousBio: Has been fighting an American over its own name for decades.
budvar.disLikeQuip: Budvar has been through worse. Lawyers, for example.

kozel-dark.description: Czech dark lager: caramel, coffee, low alcohol.
kozel-dark.humorousBio: Dark, sweet, light. And there's a goat as well.
kozel-dark.disLikeQuip: Another goat that won't forget you.

chimay-blue.description: Dark Trappist beer with plum, caramel and pepper. Gets better with age.
chimay-blue.humorousBio: Brewed by monks and ages like wine. You, less so.
chimay-blue.disLikeQuip: The Trappists remain silent. But they always do.

licher.description: Hessian Pils from the heart of nature, says the advert.
licher.humorousBio: Comes from the heart of nature. Nature didn't object.
licher.disLikeQuip: Nature has a heart. You, apparently, less so.

luebzer.description: North German Pils from Mecklenburg, fresh and clear.
luebzer.humorousBio: Mecklenburg in a bottle. Taciturn, but reliable.
luebzer.disLikeQuip: Lübzer says nothing about it. As always.

ur-krostitzer.description: Finely bitter Pils from northern Saxony with a tradition going back to the 16th century.
ur-krostitzer.humorousBio: Has a Swedish king on the label. Better not ask why.
ur-krostitzer.disLikeQuip: The Swedish king is disappointed. He moves on.

berliner-weisse.description: Sour light beer – traditionally with a shot of syrup (red or green) and a straw.
berliner-weisse.humorousBio: Comes with a straw and syrup. And isn't the least bit ashamed.
berliner-weisse.disLikeQuip: Not even with syrup? Red and green are both offended.
